Nine stars of different colours light one after another, hanging above the aimed point in a constellation. spell.irons_spellbooks_light_pollution.s: &tSecond Sun

Raises a second sun on the bearing you are facing. An enormous white disc climbs out of the horizon and fills a good part of the sky — a real light source, so everything in the world casts a second shadow that swings round as it rises. It holds high, cooling from white through gold to red as it swells, scorching enemies within 26 blocks. After about eleven seconds it goes supernova: the screen washes out, everything within 26 blocks takes 61% of its maximum health and catches fire, and the remnant collapses and goes out. Cooldown: 600 seconds.

Then it collapses, dealing 66% of maximum health within 18 blocks, throwing everything outward, and leaving three decelerating shockwaves to pass through. Cooldown: 480 seconds.

spell.irons_spellbooks_light_pollution.l: A body ninety blocks long swims in from the distance, a wave travelling down its length rather than a shape sliding across the sky. The spine arrives first, then the flanks fill out and the scales close over it — anything the body passes through takes 5.6% of its maximum health every 0.3 seconds and is thrown aside. After about six seconds the head rears, the jaws gape on their recurved fangs, and it bites once on the aimed point for 58% within 9 blocks before the body tears apart into streaming light. spell.irons_spellbooks_light_pollution.w: Plants a seed of light in the ground at the aimed point. A buttressed trunk 34 blocks tall spears up first, hitting everything within 7 blocks for 25% of its maximum health and pinning it in place. Seven roots then push out of the buttresses and race across the real terrain — climbing slopes and crossing ledges — dealing 4% within 3.2 blocks; only the advancing tips strike. Five orders of branches extend and turn up at the tips, thousands of stained-glass leaves fill the twigs, and the crown closes over into real shade before a final pulse deals 39% within 20 blocks. The whole tree hardens into pale crystal and stands for another dozen seconds before fading. Cooldown: 460 seconds.

spell.irons_spellbooks_light_pollution.g: Condenses a black hole 14 blocks above the aimed point. Outside the horizon hangs an accretion disk bent by the hole's own gravity: the disk's far side is lensed into arcs above and below the shadow while its near side crosses as a knife-thin bar, and the terrain, sky and light of your other spells bend around it too. The geometry is the real thing — the shadow is 2.6 times the horizon, the disk stops at the innermost stable circular orbit, and at roughly 4500 K there is no blue in it anywhere. While it swells, creatures within 24 blocks are dragged toward the core for 1.3% to 4.6% of maximum health every 0.4 seconds, anything pulled past the horizon is simply gone, and every other spell light in range is swallowed one by one. After about eleven seconds it reaches criticality and lets go, dealing 72% of maximum health within 20 blocks and throwing everything outward — plus 3.8% per swallowed light, up to 92%. Cooldown: 540 seconds.
Gravity: 24 blocks | Tidal: 1.3%-4.6% max health/0.4s | Lethal inside the horizon | Collapse: 72%-92%, 20 blocks | Growth: 11s | Cooldown: 540s | Mana: 2200
spell.irons_spellbooks_light_pollution.c: Sets a gravitational lens above the aimed point. The alignment closes over about two and a half seconds, after which a galaxy's light is bent around the mass in front of it into an arc spanning some three hundred degrees — the missing sixty are what give it its name. The arc is not drawn but solved for: the lens map is inverted at every pixel, which is why the ring falls where the map is singular, why the arc is thin (lensing stretches tangentially, not radially), why each of the four star-forming knots appears more than once, and why a faint counter-image sits opposite the gap. Terrain, sky and the caster's other spell light all bend around it too. The ring is the dangerous part and the interior is not: tangential magnification diverges at the Einstein radius, so that is where the light collects. Anything standing on the ring takes 2.8% of its maximum health as true damage every three quarters of a second, and when the alignment lets go the focused light is released along the ring for a further 33%. Lasts eighteen seconds.
Ring radius: 11 blocks | On the ring: 2.8% max health / 0.75s | Release: 33% along the ring only | Duration: 18s | Cooldown: 320s | Mana: 1250

spell.irons_spellbooks_light_pollution.m: Raises a microquasar above the aimed point, after SS 433. The disk assembles over about two seconds and two relativistic jets light. The disk is precessing, and that is the whole effect: every blob of plasma keeps the direction it left with while the disk turns on, so the jet is drawn out into a corkscrew. That is not a stylisation — the helix has been directly imaged in radio, and the standard kinematic model reproduces it from a precession period of about 160 days, a 20 degree cone half-angle and a jet speed of 0.26c. The two jets do not match: relativistic beaming makes the one coming toward you brighter and bluer and the one going away dimmer and redder, computed from the Doppler factor cubed rather than picked as two colours. The ejecta leave as discrete bullets, so the helix is strung with knots, each a real light casting a moving shadow. This is the only spell here dodged by timing rather than distance: the jets sweep, so holding still at a safe radius is not safe — but the precession is visible and regular. Being swept deals 4.8% of maximum health as true damage every quarter second, and when the disk finally lets go both jets fire at once for 50%. Lasts sixteen seconds.
Jet reach: 54 blocks | Sweep: 4.8% max health / 0.25s | Final: 50% | Precession: 1.5 turns | Duration: 16s | Cooldown: 380s | Mana: 1550
death.attack.microquasar: %1$s was swept through by a relativistic jet
spell.irons_spellbooks_light_pollution.h: Opens a planetary nebula at the aimed point, after NGC 7293 — the Eye of God. The white dwarf at the centre lights over about a second and a half and the envelope it threw off expands outward. The shell is not smooth gas but full of cometary knots: each a dense globule whose star-facing side is being boiled off by ionizing radiation, leaving a bright head and a tail streaming radially away. About 40,000 have been counted in the real object, each roughly 300 AU across. Two nested rings seen at an inclination give it the look of an eye, and they are different colours for a reason: the inner glows in doubly ionised oxygen, blue-green, and the outer in hydrogen and nitrogen, red — two distinct shells, not a gradient. The hazard is a wavefront rather than a radius: distance buys time, not safety, and the moment that matters is when the shell arrives. Being swept deals 7.2% of maximum health as true damage every three tenths of a second, and when the shell reaches its full extent the star collapses for 42% across the whole nebula. Lasts seventeen seconds.
Shell reach: 30 blocks (outer ring 42) | Wavefront: 7.2% max health / 0.3s | Collapse: 42% | Duration: 17s | Cooldown: 340s | Mana: 1350
death.attack.helix_nebula: %1$s was engulfed by an expanding nebula
spell.irons_spellbooks_light_pollution.m: Calls up a magnetar above the aimed point, after SGR 1806-20 — a neutron star with a field around 10^15 gauss, the strongest magnetism known. The star forms over about eighteen tenths of a second and closed dipole field lines thread out from its poles. The loops come from the real dipole relation r = r0 sin^2(theta), so they are the closed curves a dipole actually makes rather than arcs drawn to look magnetic: leaving a pole along the axis, bulging at the equator, closing on the other pole. The hazard is a set of curved loops, not a sphere: only the lines discharge, and the gaps between them are safe — this is the only spell here where where you stand matters more than how far away you are. The magnetosphere winds tighter as it goes, the lines twisting and shifting from cold violet toward white-hot with packets of charge sliding along them, all of which is the field visibly loading. Touching a line deals 2.4% of maximum health as true damage every four tenths of a second. After about eleven and a half seconds the magnetosphere rearranges itself all at once — the real event in 2004 was the most powerful giant flare on record and ionised Earth's upper atmosphere from fifty thousand light years away — for 78% within 22 blocks. That is the heaviest single hit here outside the two dedicated executions, but the wind-up is long and bright enough that nobody is caught by it unwarned. Lasts fifteen seconds.
Field reach: 19 blocks | Touching a line: 2.4% max health / 0.4s | Flare: 78%, 22 blocks | Wind-up: 11.5s | Duration: 15s | Cooldown: 500s | Mana: 1900
death.attack.magnetar: %1$s was erased by a magnetospheric rearrangement
spell.irons_spellbooks_light_pollution.t: Sets a tidal disruption event above the aimed point. After about two and a third seconds a star is pulled open — and the star is the subject, not the hole: the tidal field stretches it along its orbit into one enormously long, thin stream of debris that wraps back around. Roughly half the debris ends up bound and returns; the rest is flung away and never comes back. The returning material lights the flare, and its fallback rate declines as t^(-5/3), the classic signature of a disruption — so the brightness curve here is computed from that exponent rather than drawn by hand. The stream does not pull or detonate, it lashes: the leading tip sits deepest in the tidal field and is the hottest and thinnest, running blue-white, while the trailing end is cooler and thicker and runs red. Being lashed deals 5.8% of maximum health as true damage every quarter second, and when the bound debris returns the accretion flare deals 47% within 20 blocks. Lasts eighteen seconds.
Stream: 62 blocks | Lash: 5.8% max health / 0.25s | Flare: 47%, 20 blocks | Duration: 18s | Cooldown: 520s | Mana: 1950
death.attack.tidal_disruption: %1$s was flayed by a stream of stellar debris
spell.irons_spellbooks_light_pollution.q: Fires a quasar jet above the aimed point, after M87. One jet, not two: at these speeds relativistic beaming makes the receding one so faint it is effectively invisible, which is why the famous images show a single needle out of the nucleus. It does not precess and does not wander — a straight collimated beam. The channel is visible the whole time but only the knots hit. They race along it at an apparent speed from beta_app = beta sin(theta) / (1 - beta cos(theta)), which at a Lorentz factor of 10 and a viewing angle of 17 degrees comes out at almost exactly six times light speed — the figure actually tracked for M87's knots. The superluminal motion is therefore computed, not asserted. The far end rams the surrounding medium and builds a hotspot inside a diffuse radio lobe. A knot passing through deals 6.8% of maximum health as true damage; the terminal hotspot deals 53% within 10 blocks. Lasts seventeen seconds.
Jet: 72 blocks | Knot: 6.8% max health | Apparent speed: ~6c | Hotspot: 53%, 10 blocks | Duration: 17s | Cooldown: 560s | Mana: 2100

spell.irons_spellbooks_light_pollution.p: Lights a Wolf-Rayet binary above the aimed point, after WR 104. Two hot stars whose winds collide, condensing dust along the shock and trailing it out behind the orbit as a spiral — imaged directly with aperture masking on Keck, turning with a period of about 220 days. It is an Archimedean spiral, not a Keplerian one: dust leaves at a steady wind speed while the binary turns at a steady rate, so the pitch is constant and successive arms are evenly spaced, where a disk has material at different radii going round at different speeds. There is empty space between the arms rather than a filled annulus, and this is dust at a few hundred kelvin, so it is red-brown and never approaches white. The whole pattern rotates rigidly, and that is the mechanic: the safe gaps between the arms travel with it, so a gap is only safe until the next arm sweeps into it. Being in the dust deals 2.1% of maximum health as true damage every fifth of a second, and the binary's final flare-up deals 36% within 26 blocks. Lasts fifteen seconds.
Spiral: 26 blocks | Dust: 2.1% max health / 0.2s | Flare: 36%, 26 blocks | Rotation: 1.4 turns | Duration: 15s | Cooldown: 280s | Mana: 1100
death.attack.pinwheel: %1$s was scoured by a spiral of carbon dust
spell.irons_spellbooks_light_pollution.c: Unfolds the Crab Nebula above the aimed point — M1, the remnant of the supernova recorded by Chinese and Japanese astronomers in 1054. It is two things at once, and the fact that they are separate is the whole spell: a cage of filaments on the surface of the shell with nothing between them, and inside that cage a synchrotron wind nebula driven by the pulsar at the centre, a different colour and a different texture. The filaments are line emission from cooling gas — sharp, knotted, red shot through with green. The wind nebula is synchrotron radiation from relativistic electrons — smooth, structureless, blue-white. Unlike the World Tree, which is a solid branching from a root, this is a hollow cage over a void, and a player can stand inside one. So it is a trap rather than a radius: outside is safe, the filaments sting, and the inside is where the pulsar's wind pulses — and leaving means crossing the cage again. Touching a filament deals 1.6% of maximum health as true damage every 0.35s; inside the cage the wind deals 2.6% every half second; and the remnant letting go at the end deals 30% across the whole shell. Lasts sixteen seconds.
Shell: 21 blocks | Filaments: 1.6% max health / 0.35s | Interior wind: 2.6% / 0.5s | Collapse: 30% | Duration: 16s | Cooldown: 260s | Mana: 1050
